items.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011
items.q: I read a story by Leonard Feather

ctx.x: Well it sort of grew. The idea for “The Real Ambassadors” really came after they did the State Department tour. And I was so impressed with how jazz and music was received in cultures that were different from ours, and what it actually meant at that period in that part of the world. In Poland, for example, jazz just became this symbol of the freedom that they wanted and were seeking. And so it was an underground movement that for some time was forbidden, and by the time, in 1958, when the quartet went there, it…

how do you express that? How do you get that idea over to the public? Then I decided one way perhaps would be to put it into a musical so that you would have jazz musicians on the stage. I love the sense of humor and I thought if you could just capture some of that, it would be so great, and the public would like it. So that’s how it came about, and then getting to Louis Armstrong and talking to him, and much to our surprise he really took it very, very seriously and really wanted to do it.
